commitResults.messageBody: Update AboutUs.md with Tran Duc Thien's details

Commands need a consistent way to read and display dates and months.
Centralising this in DateUtil keeps the format (DD-MM-YYYY / MM-YYYY)
in one place and uses ResolverStyle.STRICT so invalid dates such as
31-02-2026 are rejected instead of silently adjusted.

TripJioException lets parsing errors carry a user-friendly message
up to the UI layer.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add Ui class for user interaction
commitResults.messageBody:
All console input and output goes through Ui so that other classes
do not print directly. Ui takes its input and output streams through
a constructor, so tests can feed it fake input and capture its output;
the no-argument constructor uses System.in and System.out.

readCommand() returns "exit" when input runs out, so the app stops
cleanly instead of crashing when run with redirected input.

Also adds the TripJio welcome banner, the goodbye message and a
formatMoney helper for displaying amounts as "$1,234.50".

The exception, ui and util packages were at the top level of
src/main/java, while the main class lives in seedu.tripjio. Putting
everything under seedu.tripjio gives the project one root package,
avoids name clashes with other libraries' generic "ui"/"util"
packages, and matches the structure used by the course templates.

Only package and import statements change; there are no behaviour
changes in this commit.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add Expense model, Category and MoneyUtil
commitResults.messageBody:
Expense and Category are the core data that the budget, trip and
statistics features will read from. Expense.getAmount() is the single
place those features get an amount from, so SplitExpense can later
override it to return only the user's share.

Display and storage follow the User Guide: dates use DD-MM-YYYY via
DateUtil, and amounts use "$1,234.50" for display and "1234.50" in
data/tripjio.txt. fromStorageString() validates every field and throws
TripJioException for a bad line, so Storage can skip it with a warning
instead of loading wrong data or crashing.

MoneyUtil holds amount validation (more than 0, at most 1,000,000)
and formatting. formatMoney moves there from Ui so that the model
does not depend on the UI layer. Formatting uses Locale.ROOT so the
storage file stays readable on computers with other locales.

Smaller fixes:
- Category uses Locale.ROOT when changing case.
- DateUtil trims input before parsing.
- The goodbye message matches the User Guide ("Safe travels!").

SplitExpense records a group bill and stores only the user's share in
the inherited amount field, so budget, trip and statistics code gets
the right value from getAmount() without an override and the share is
kept in one place.

The equal share is rounded to cents with the new
MoneyUtil.roundToCents, as the User Guide requires, so totals match
the amounts shown to the user. The class comment records the rules
the team agreed for editing the full bill.

Loading from storage, setAmount, toString and toStorageString are
left as TODOs for D.

ExpenseList holds every expense and gives the budget, trip and
statistics features one place to read from. Indexes start from 1 to
match the numbers shown by the list command, and get/delete share one
checkIndex method so the error messages stay consistent.

Totals always use getAmount(), so split expenses count only the
user's share, and are rounded to cents so floating-point errors
(e.g. 0.1 + 0.2) cannot push a total across a budget threshold.
getAll() returns a copy so callers cannot modify the list directly.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add month storage format to DateUtil
commitResults.messageBody:
formatMonth() returns "December 2026" for display, but budgets are
stored in the data file as "12-2026". formatMonthForStorage() reuses
MONTH_FORMAT, so whatever it writes can be read back by parseMonth().

Budget keeps a default budget and per-month budgets in a TreeMap, so
months are saved to the data file in order. Amounts are validated with
MoneyUtil, the same rule as Expense. Budgets are loaded one line at a
time, so an invalid line can be skipped with a warning without losing
the others, as the User Guide requires.

BudgetChecker returns the warning text instead of printing it through
Ui, so the model does not depend on the UI layer and the warnings are
easy to unit test. This also removes the dependency on the missing
AppState class, which stopped the project from compiling.

The lookup, storage and warning logic are left as TODOs for B.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add Trip, Statistics and AppState placeholders
commitResults.messageBody:
Trip stores the current trip's start and end dates. set() asserts that
the end is not before the start, because the trip command is expected
to report invalid input to the user before calling it. Loading and
saving are left as TODOs for C, following the same one-line-at-a-time
loading as Budget so a bad line can be skipped.

Statistics is an empty placeholder for C's stats commands.

AppState groups the expense list, budget and trip into one object, so
commands and storage take a single parameter. It has no setters;
changes go through the methods of each part.

Every command with prefixes (d/, a/, dt/, ...) needs the same parsing,
so ArgumentParser splits the arguments into a preamble and the values
of each prefix once, for all team members to reuse. dt/ and my/ are
matched before d/ and m/ so they are not misread.

It also provides shared checks so input rules live in one place:
parseAmount checks the format and leaves the range to MoneyUtil,
parseIndex rejects non-positive and out-of-range numbers, and
parseDescription rejects '/' and '|', which would break prefix parsing
and the storage file.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add Command, Parser, help and exit
commitResults.messageBody:
Command is the base class of every command (Command pattern).
isMutating() and getAffectedMonth() let the main loop save the data
and check the budget after a command, so individual commands do not
repeat that logic.

Parser only reads the command word and hands the arguments to each
feature's own parser, so each team member changes a single line in
Parser. Features that are not ready yet share one "not available"
error; the grouped cases contain only comments, so checkstyle's
FallThrough rule is not triggered.

HelpCommand lists the formats from the User Guide's Command Summary.
ExitCommand is marked as mutating so the data is saved before exit.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add add, list, edit and delete commands
commitResults.messageBody:
ExpenseCommandParser checks everything that only needs the input text
(missing or repeated prefixes, formats, future dates, edit with no
fields), so the commands receive values that are already valid.

list loops with a counter so filtered results still show each
expense's original index, which the User Guide says can be used with
edit and delete. edit changes the amount first because it is the only
setter that can fail (e.g. a split bill below the user's own share),
so a failed edit leaves the expense unchanged. edit reports the month
after the change, so the budget of the new month is checked.

Output follows the User Guide. The messages for an empty list and a
filter with no matches are not in the User Guide yet.

Storage saves all data to data/tripjio.txt in the block format from
the User Guide, creating the folder if needed, and loads it back at
start-up.

load() never throws: a missing or unreadable file starts with no data,
and each line is loaded in its own try/catch so an invalid line is
skipped with a warning (with its line number) while the rest still
loads, as the User Guide requires. UTF-8 is always used so
descriptions such as "Phở" survive on every platform.

Note: until split expenses, budgets and the trip implement their
loading and saving, their lines are skipped on load and are not
written back on the next save.

TripJio loads the data, shows the welcome message and then reads and
runs commands until exit. After each successful command it checks the
budget of the affected month and saves the data if it changed; a
failed command shows an error and skips both steps.

When input runs out, Ui returns "exit", so the app also stops
cleanly and saves when run with redirected input.
